module_imports — transitive, cycle-safe, reading live ImportStmt edges —
lived in cursor.mn, which imports infer, so the comment-reference gate
could not reach it. Resolution fell back to the link's flattened env,
where smap_get(cdix, name) answers "this name exists somewhere in the
link" while SYNTAX asks whether an EDGE exists. The family is homed in
graph.mn beside module_path_of_span (the DAG bottom — the reason that
comment already gives), with module_reaches(from_h, target_h) as the
handle-facing entry, since a node's module is stamped at its mint.

A two-module fixture refuted this landing's own premise mid-build. leaf.mn
carries a comment naming a decl in the module that IMPORTS it, plus a name
that exists nowhere. Addressing leaf.mn:3 — making leaf the entry —
reports both. check top.mn, where leaf is merely imported, reports
neither, and neither do compile or verify. A name that exists nowhere
going unreported rules resolution out: the gate judges only the ENTRY

suppression — deliberate, and right for a user verb.

inside a single module. comment-refs: 0 was not a measurement that read
zero; it was one that could not read anything else.

Landed here is the resolution half, correct though masked by that
suppression. Banked is the coverage half, and it is a split rather than
a second walk: crc_walk already computes the misses as [(handle, name)]
before crc_judge_dollars filters and reports them.

NRecordRowBound carries Option(Int) now: None terminates the chain —
these fields and no more — and Some(v) continues it at another row var
whose residual is not yet known. Every writer passes None today, so this
is behaviour-identical, confirmed by re-running the arc's repro unchanged
at 7. open_record_full_fields gained its chase arm for the linked case,
which reaches a still-free tail and floors, so the reader is ready before
the writer exists.

The arity change is the point, and it is why this shape was chosen over a
new node kind. The previous attempt died because a row walk's catch-all
silently crossed a sort boundary; a new kind is found only where matches
are exhaustive, and a catch-all is exactly where it is not. An arity
change is a compile error at every site — twenty-one across eight files —
so the enumeration belongs to the compiler rather than to me.

The stamp this pays: unify_two_open_records closes both tails to the other
side's exclusive fields, which reads as "and nothing further" and bakes a
field offset over a partial set. The repair is to link the tails, and the
march's constraint from last iteration is that the link must live in the
row sort. This slot is that vocabulary.

Not yet true, said plainly: nothing reads Some, so the silent wrong is
untouched. `fn pick(u: {zeta: Int, ...}) = u.zeta` over {alpha: 7,
zeta: 9} still answers 7. The vocabulary is the floor the fix stands on,
not the fix. The writer flip is a TRANSITION by construction — the
refuted attempt measured 131477 diff lines for the same semantic change —
so the m4 leg gets watched from the first run.

mentl/fd40655:
SYNTAX's product law says a handler's config list IS a parameter product,
and a product field carries a default; the lathe lagged. Measured through
the pinned boot: handler give(k = 7) refused at parse (expected ), found
=; exit 1, zero WAT) — the lathe-lag that keeps a root handler's defaults
off its decl and re-typed at every install site.

The config carrier goes [String] -> [TParam], the fn-param carrier, so
the default has ONE representation (the TParam's fifth slot) and ONE fill
(resolve_call_args) for fns and handlers alike. parse_config_params
parses name [= default] per param, mirroring parse_one_param's scalar
branch; mint_handler_config_tparams preserves name and default while
minting the graph var, and chase_params/subst_params already carry the
default through generalize/instantiate via param_with_ty, so both the
pre-registered and the re-generalized scheme keep it. register_handler
types each default at its one home, the handler's own parameter scope,
unifying it into the param's var under a DefaultReason edge — a bare
~> h install has no call node to splice through, so the decl is the
scope that grounds it. At lower, extract_handler_config_args resolves
the install's product through resolve_call_args, the same read infer's
CallExpr path takes, so the two phases see one positional order by
construction: explicit args place, labels skip over, absent fields draw
their decl default; a bare VarRef install of a config'd handler is the
zero-arg product, gated on HandlerKind so a tee over a plain fn value
keeps its passthrough. Name readers project via lower_param_names and
cl_param_names; the formatter renders name = default back; graph.mn's
orphaned copy of the mint comment is deleted.

The four product faces discriminate in tests/frontier/
mn-handler-config-default.mn (bare-fill 8, explicit 16, omitting-parens
6, labeled skip-over 12 = 42), RED on the pinned boot and 42 through the
new wheel. An earlier-param-referencing default refuses E_MissingVariable
e
mentl/fd74409:
describe(x) = "val: " ++ to_string(x) at a Float call prints the address
(val: 1048600, the first cell past heap base), measured. Two stacked
causes: the worthiness witness is binop-only, so a to_string call never
demands a twin; and even a twin could not fix it, because
lower_to_string_dispatch reads the operand's floor type and commits the
word-show path into the LowIR — an emit-time bracket cannot re-make a
decision lower already minted. Same for hash. Banked as
tests/repro/mn-generic-show-lower-dispatch.mn beside the nested-lambda
face; the ultimate is band D's show/compare-hash-leaf-as-lowered-LFn
work, which moves those type reads to emit where the spec_wty bracket
specializes them like every other read.
mentl/fd7cf73:
Iteration 3 made compute_escaping_rows' write side (callee-name to
base-position resolution) O(1); the READ side stayed O(n^2).
evidence_effects_of and can_yield receive callee_handle, discard it,
extract the name via callee_name_of_handle, and linear-scan the esc_rows
name-to-row assoc-list once per call site (escaping_row -> ls_escaping_of
-> esc_assoc). perf pinned that scan at 72% of the post-esc-setup compile
— the Carried-Truth violation in the flesh: the caller holds the edge
(callee_handle) and re-derives the row by string anyway.

esc_rows is now a 4096-bucket str_hash name-to-row index, built once at
ls_register_escaping (build_esc_index) and read O(1) at every call site
(esc_index_get). The handler state inits to make_list(4096) so a lookup
before register returns None rather than trapping OOB on list_index([],
b); buckets are reverse-inserted so a name's first match is byte-identical
to the old forward scan (base names are unique, so the order is moot but
the invariant holds regardless).

m3-gen 226s to 56s (a 4x single-iteration drop — the read side was the
dominant remainder), m2 == m3 byte-identical (468421 lines; escaping rows
drive ev-slot dispatch, so byte-identity is the correctness check), 8/8
rungs, 66/66 micros, 5/5 crown. Cumulative across four perf-found O(1)
fixes: 1400s to 56s, ~25x, every step byte-identical.

The str_hash index is the O(1) waypoint; the deletion-ultimate is
Hbeta.lower.esc-row-on-node (the escaping row an edge on the callee's
node, read by following callee_handle — the side-table and the name
extraction gone), generalized by Hbeta.perf.name-is-handle (intern names
to handles at lex → the whole str_hash-index class becomes i32.eq or
dissolves). Both named in PLAN §5.O layers 1-2.

mentl/fd4bf04:
The base case of insert_field_sorted_at returned [field] instead of
sorted ++ [field]. When a field needed to be inserted at the END of
an already-sorted list (because no earlier field compared greater),
the preceding elements vanished.

For a 2-field record with source order [later, earlier], this caused
the first insertion to drop one field. For a 5-field record like
lower_program_typed's own handler [is_ctor, find_rewrite, is_global,
is_state_var, fresh_id], it silently dropped fresh_id from the record
every time the compiler ran, so:

  - __ev_op_fresh_id was never installed by lower_program_typed's
    handler — it stayed at the default dummy that returns 0
  - Every call to fresh_id() returned 0
  - Every lower_lambda_inner call built name_0 regardless of count
  - All inner fns (go, lambda_*) collided on name_0
  - The function table kept exactly one copy with arbitrary arity
  - iterate's closure stored the fn_idx of parse_int's go_0 (closure,
    i, acc) while call_indirect expected fn1 (closure, i)
  - wasm trap: indirect call type mismatch

Found via the minimal reproducer:

  effect LC { noop() -> (), fresh() -> Int }
  fn body() = { noop(); fresh() + fresh() + fresh() + fresh() }
  println(to_string(handle { body() } with state = 0 {
    noop()  => resume(()),
    fresh() => resume(state) with state = state + 1
  }))

Rust VM before fix: 0 (every fresh() returns 0)
After fix:          6 (0+1+2+3, state increments correctly)

If the arm order is swapped so fresh comes first, the bug doesn't
manifest — because alphabetical order ["fresh","noop"] is already
achieved by prepending, never hitting the broken base case.

Verification:
  - All 4 crucibles still pass (hello, ultimate, counter, check)
  - minimal repro: 0 -> 6
  - lux lower of the repro now shows #record:fresh,noop(...) with
    both lambda bodies present and fresh's stash-then-update-then-
    return sequence intact

This unblocks the stage-2 self-compile story: with fresh_id actually
incrementi

noodles/fd44009:
A key signature is a promise about letters: seven degrees, seven
letters, in order from the tonic's. Chord names now ride that
arithmetic - F# major runs F# G#m A#m B C# D#m E#dim, with the
seventh degree spelled E# because F is already taken - and the
piano roll's noteName puts an in-scale pitch in its letter's
octave while chromatic visitors take the signature side's
spelling. Verified across all 72 mode/key pairs: seven distinct
letters each, never a double accidental (the side-spelled tonics
from keyDisplayName guarantee it). This ends the A#/Bb split the
circle made visible and is the prerequisite the staff projection
stands on: an engraved 3-flat signature cannot say A#.
